finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: POST /restore passes attacker-supplied base64 `state` param directly to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and RCE via Ruby gadget chains.

trace.note: route POST /restore, no auth filter or before block
state.inspect invoked on the deserialized object (can also trigger gadget methods)

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no signature/HMAC on the payload, no class allowlist, no size limit; Base64.decode64 is not a validation. File has no before filters. Also if params[:state] is missing, nil raises an error (only DoS, not a control).

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-7 shows the unauthenticated POST /restore route passing Base64-decoded params[:state] straight into Marshal.load at app.rb:6, with no auth, before filter, signature, or class allowlist anywhere in the single-file app.
